analysis: Both changed files are live, env-gated test files under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Live (DARKBLOOM_LIVE_MLX_TESTS=1 plus a model-specific gate). The only changes are exhaustive-switch updates for a new `.logprobs` stream event case: GemmaToolCallLiveTests.swift line 264 (`case .info, .logprobs: break`) and Qwen36ProductionCanaryTests.swift (head lines 394-395, `case .logprobs: break`). These tests discard the event, so they add no production code path, data exposure, authorization or attestation change, and no runtime attack surface. The test-only changes do not touch the encrypted prefix cache (T-041) or the coordinator/provider channel (TB-002), which the production code owns. The visible diff does not show how the new `.logprobs` event is produced or whether the production server path might leak logprobs, for example through unencrypted fields or the cache-hit timing oracle. That implementation lives in non-supplied source files, so I record it as an unverified contract for integration or other batches rather than a finding. Nothing in these files indicates a regression.
